NONE: A1 to put or take food into the mouth, chew it (= crush it with the teeth), and swallow it
吃

example: Do you eat meat?
你吃肉嗎？
When I've got a cold, I don't feel like eating.
我感冒時沒有食慾。
We usually eat (= have a meal) at about seven o'clock.
我們通常在七點前後吃飯。

NONE: B2 to eat all the food that you have been given
吃完，吃光

example: Be a good boy and eat up your vegetables.
好孩子，乖，把蔬菜都吃了。

NONE: › If a bad memory or feeling eats away at someone, it makes them feel more and more unhappy.
長期困擾；煩擾
› to gradually damage or destroy something
逐漸毀掉；侵蝕；損耗
› to admit that you were wrong
認錯；道歉

example: After boasting that his company could outperform the industry's best, he's been forced to eat humble pie.
他吹噓他的公司可以勝過業內最好的企業，但之後，他就不得不承認言過其實了。

NONE: › to have a meal at home rather than in a restaurant
在家吃飯
› to use or take away a large part of something valuable, such as money or time
消耗，花掉，耗費（金錢或時間）

example: The high cost of living in London is eating into my savings.
倫敦生活費用太高了，我的積蓄都花了不少了。

NONE: › to always eat a small amount of food
吃得很少；食量極小

example: You eat like a bird – I don't know how you stay healthy.
你吃得太少了——我不知道你怎麼能保持健康。

NONE: › to always eat a lot of food
吃得很多；食量極大

example: She's so thin, yet she eats like a horse.
她那麼瘦，可是食量極大。

NONE: B1 to eat in a restaurant
去餐廳吃飯；在外用餐

example: When I lived in Spain, I used to eat out all the time.
我住在西班牙的時候，天天去外面吃飯。

NONE: › to criticize someone very angrily
憤怒地批評…

example: If we get our facts wrong we'll be eaten alive by the press.
如果我們把事實弄錯了，媒體會對我們大肆發難的。

NONE: › to be able to very easily control or defeat someone
不費吹灰之力地制伏（或打敗）

example: He eats people like you for breakfast.
像你這樣的人，他不費吹灰之力就制得服服貼貼了。

NONE: › to eat a lot of the food someone has in their house
把…吃窮；吃光…的家當
› to use or take away a large part of something valuable
（大量）耗費，損耗

example: A big old car like that eats up petrol.
像那樣的老式大型車很耗油。

NONE: › If you say "eat your heart out" followed by the name of a famous person, you are joking that you are even better than that person.
（後接一個名人的名字，開玩笑地說比其還要強）比你強多了，你算老幾

example: I'm singing in the village production of Tosca next month - eat your heart out Pavarotti!
下個月我們村裡劇團要上演《托斯卡》，我會上臺一展歌喉——帕華洛帝，我比你強多了！

NONE: › to admit that something you said before was wrong
承認自己說錯了話

example: Sam said it would never sell, but when he sees these sales figures he'll have to eat his words.
山姆曾說這個永遠不會有銷路。可是他要是看到這些銷售數字，就得承認自己錯了。

NONE: › Food that is eatable is good enough to eat, but not excellent.
（不算很好但）還可以吃的；能食用的，可吃的

example: Compare
edible

NONE: › If someone is eaten up with/by a negative emotion, they are experiencing it very strongly.
被（某種消極情緒）所折磨；內心充滿（某種消極情緒）

example: He was so eaten up with guilt, he became ill.
心中的愧疚無時無刻不在折磨著他，最後他病倒了。

NONE: › a restaurant
餐館；飲食店

example: We met in a little eatery just off the main road.
我們是在大路邊的一家小飯館相遇的。

NONE: › an apple that can be eaten uncooked, rather than cooked
（非烹調用）可生吃的蘋果

example: Compare
cooking apple

NONE: › a mental illness in which people eat far too little or far too much food and are unhappy with their bodies
飲食失調症，進食障礙
› a small amount of food
（少量）食物

example: Would you like some eats?
你要不要來點吃的？
